elaine (docs): quick heads-up — noticed a schema vs example mismatch on the /v1/generate reference. the python snippet uses `temperature: 0.7` but the request schema currently lists `temperature` as an integer (type: integer).

samir (eng): ah yep that will break client validation for SDKs that strict-validate. good catch. do you want the schema changed to number or update the examples to ints?

elaine (docs): leaning toward allowing number/float in schema (temperature is conceptually a float). i filed a docs PR with the minimal change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2824 — it updates the OpenAPI param type to `number` and adjusts examples where needed.

jordan (sdks): pinged. i can adapt the python/json schema validators, but prefer changing the openapi to `number` so all clients get consistent contracts. any breaking concerns?

maria (product): +1 to `number`. we should add a short migration note in the changelog so integrators know floats are now supported (and mention older SDKs may validate differently).

elaine (docs): added a changelog snippet in the PR description. also added an inline example showing both `0.7` and `1.0` to illustrate accepted formats.

samir (eng): quick review left. main question: do we need to bump the spec version? might be minor but worth tagging as patch.

jordan (sdks): i ran the new schema against the python validator locally — looks fine. snippet i used:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/generic-1",
  "prompt": "Write a haiku about coffee",
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "max_new_tokens": 64
}
```

jordan (sdks): also tested `temperature: 1` (int) — still valid. so number handles both.

deploy-bot: docs preview deployed — https://deploy-previews.redwood-inference.com/docs/pr-2824 — preview will auto-expire in 48h.

elaine (docs): awesome. can someone from eng merge after CI passes? i want this live before next SDK release. :pray:

samir (eng): i'll merge after CI green and add a spec patch tag. scheduling for 30m unless any blockers.

maria (product): noted for release notes. thanks all! :tada:
